_meta.indication: KYGEVVI is indicated for the treatment of thymidine kinase 2 deficiency (TK2d) in adults and pediatric patients with an age of symptom onset on or before 12 years.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Trial 1 (MT-1621-101) — with supporting retrospective chart-review studies Study 1 and Study 2 and an expanded access program
pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 2 clinical study (Trial 1), supported by retrospective chart-review studies and an expanded access program
pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, open-label, single-arm study; survival in treated patients compared with an untreated external control group of matched patients (78 matched pairs).
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and pediatric patients with genetically confirmed thymidine kinase 2 deficiency (TK2d) with age of symptom onset ≤12 years, previously treated with pyrimidine nucleosides.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall survival (survival compared to matched untreated external control) — the primary efficacy endpoint.
pivotal_trials.n: 78 treated patients vs 78 matched untreated external control patients in the survival analysis.
pivotal_trials.result: Significant survival benefit: hazard ratio 0.14 (95% CI 0.04, 0.39); risk of death reduced by ~86% (95% CI 61%, 96%); deaths 3 (3.8%) treated vs 28 (35.9%) untreated.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5%) are diarrhea, abdominal pain, vomiting, and increased ALT and AST. In treated patients (N=47): diarrhea 72% (34), abdominal pain 23% (11), vomiting 21% (10), ALT increased 21% (10), AST increased 17% (8). Dose reductions occurred in 22% and permanent discontinuation in 9% of patients.
target_moa: KYGEVVI is a combination of two pyrimidine nucleosides (doxecitine and doxribtimine) that provides a balanced increase in deoxycytidine and deoxythymidine, bypassing the impaired TK2 salvage pathway; incorporation into mitochondrial DNA increases mtDNA copy number to restore mtDNA synthesis in TK2 deficiency.
modality: A combination of two pyrimidine nucleosides (doxecitine and doxribtimine).

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation was granted for the combination of dCMP and dTMP for the treatment of TK2d on July 7, 2016.

summary.text: KYGEVVI was approved via a traditional (not accelerated) approval under a 505(b)(2) NDA with priority review in the Division of Rare Diseases and Medical Genetics. The product had orphan drug designation for TK2d, and the sponsor was granted a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher. Effectiveness was based on an external-control survival comparison supported by mechanistic confirmatory evidence.
